learningObjectives: Explain how the passed deadline interval differs from the goal and deadline
Configure a passed deadline interval to repeat a fixed number of times or until the work completes
Recognize that the passed deadline interval is configured only in Dev Studio on the SLA Rule
Apply the Urgency cap (max 100) and escalation Actions to drive overdue work to completion

elements.description: Defines further scheduled action for still-open work after its deadline. Repetition follows the configured event count or Assignment completion policy; it is not automatically unlimited.

elements.text: Think of a reminder series with a stop condition: the first overdue reminder follows the deadline, and later reminders occur at configured intervals. Set the reminder count; do not confuse reaching a priority ceiling with completing the task.

elements.description: Key distinction from goal and deadline intervals:
items: Goal and Deadline fire ONCE only
Passed deadline interval can REPEAT — a FIXED NUMBER OF TIMES or UNTIL the Assignment is completed
On each repeat: can increase Urgency and trigger escalation Actions

elements.description: Configure the passed deadline interval in Dev Studio on the SLA Rule. App Studio-created SLAs auto-generate an SLA Rule — goal/deadline come from App Studio, but the passed deadline interval must be added on the Rule.

elements.caption: Overdue intervals are separate from the goal and deadline. Each applicable event applies configured actions, within the event limit or until Assignment completion.

elements.description: The linked v7 challenge opens the Review Step’s SLA in Dev Studio, limits passed deadline events to six, sets a 15-minute interval, adds +10 urgency and selects Notify Manager. After this customization, goals and deadlines are edited through the SLA Rule as well.

Urgency is capped at 100. Once an Assignment reaches Urgency 100, Pega IGNORES further Urgency increments — but CONTINUES other escalation Actions. Example: if Urgency is already 100, Pega skips the increase yet still sends the notification.
Actions triggered on every passed deadline interval (same as goal/deadline):
items: Reassign (to another user or Work Queue)

elements.title: Escalation Action Decisions

examPitfalls.title: Passed deadline interval REPEATS
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Unlike the one-time goal and deadline, the passed deadline interval repeats — a fixed number of times or until the work is completed.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Set the interval, event count, stop condition and actions explicitly.

examPitfalls.title: Configured only in Dev Studio
examPitfalls.trapDescription: The passed deadline interval is set ONLY in Dev Studio on the SLA Rule; App Studio's goal/deadline panel does not expose it.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: App Studio SLA creates the SLA Rule; add the passed deadline interval there in Dev Studio.

examPitfalls.title: Urgency caps at 100 (but actions continue)
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Questions ask what happens when Urgency reaches 100 and the Deadline continues to pass. Candidates say escalation stops. Urgency is capped at 100 — it does not go higher — but configured escalation Actions continue to fire at each interval even after the cap is reached.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Don't assume escalation stops at 100 — only the Urgency increase is ignored, not the Actions.

examPitfalls.title: Goal/deadline vs. passed deadline
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Goal and deadline define on-time targets and fire once; the passed deadline interval handles work that is already late and repeats.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: On-time = goal/deadline; late-work = passed deadline interval + escalation Actions.

examPitfalls.title: Escalation Actions set
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Distinguish configured notifications, reassignment and resolution from urgency adjustments. Do not assume an arbitrary processing Rule is a standard action in every editor.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Know the set: Notify (assignee/manager/participants) · Reassign (user/Work Queue) · Resolve the Case.

examPitfalls.title: Passed deadline interval is NOT the SLA Deadline
examPitfalls.trapDescription: A question describes an SLA with a Deadline of 2 days and a 'Passed Deadline' repeat interval of 1 hour. Candidates say the Deadline is 1 hour. The Passed Deadline interval defines how often the escalation action repeats AFTER the Deadline — the Deadline itself is the 2-day threshold.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Both deadline and passed deadline settings belong to the SLA Rule; the latter is not a separate Passed Deadline Interval Rule.

examPitfalls.title: Escalation actions require explicit configuration
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Questions ask whether escalation happens automatically once a Deadline is set. Candidates say yes. A Deadline alone does not trigger any action — escalation actions (Notify, Reassign, etc.) must be explicitly configured on the SLA rule.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Configure both urgency adjustments and any required notification or reassignment. A deadline does not establish an automatic increment or notification without configuration.

practiceQuiz.scenario: An Assignment's SLA deadline has already passed but the work is still incomplete. Which SLA component continues to fire at recurring intervals to keep escalating the Assignment?

options.text: Passed deadline interval — recurring overdue events within the configured event limit or until Assignment completion
The goal interval — the goal threshold fires once before the deadline and then stops escalating
A Data Transform — a Data Transform is scheduled to run on a timer and updates the urgency field directly
An Access Role — the Access Role's time limit re-checks permissions on each elapsed interval and escalates when expired

practiceQuiz.hint: After the deadline passes, what keeps escalating? The repeating passed-deadline interval.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Passed deadline defines the recurring schedule for overdue work, subject to its event limit or completion. The goal is an earlier one-time milestone, not the recurring overdue schedule.

optionExplanations.A: Passed deadline defines the recurring schedule for overdue work, subject to its event limit or completion.
optionExplanations.B: The goal is an earlier one-time milestone, not the recurring overdue schedule.
optionExplanations.C: A Data Transform does not itself define this SLA recurrence.
optionExplanations.D: An Access Role does not define the elapsed SLA intervals.

practiceQuiz.scenario: An insurance claim has a 4-hour SLA goal and a 12-hour deadline. At hour 4 (goal missed), the SA wants an email sent to the supervisor. At hour 12 (deadline), the SA wants the Case reassigned to a senior specialist. Can these two DIFFERENT actions be triggered at different SLA milestones?

options.text: Yes — the Goal and Deadline are separate milestones, each with their own independently configurable escalation actions; different actions fire at each threshold
No — all SLA escalation actions must be identical at both the Goal and Deadline; if you notify at the Goal, you must also notify at the Deadline
No — escalation actions can only be configured on the Deadline, not the Goal; the Goal only increases urgency without triggering actions
Yes, but only in Dev Studio — App Studio only allows the same action type (notification only or reassignment only) across all milestones

practiceQuiz.hint: Goal and Deadline are separate milestones. Can each have its own action?
practiceQuiz.rationale: Each milestone can have its own configured response. Notification and reassignment serve different purposes. The milestones are not required to use identical escalation actions.

optionExplanations.A: Each milestone can have its own configured response. Notification and reassignment serve different purposes.
optionExplanations.B: The milestones are not required to use identical escalation actions.
optionExplanations.C: The goal can have actions as well as urgency adjustments.
optionExplanations.D: The scenario does not establish the proposed blanket Studio restriction.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A compliance officer says: 'When a regulatory filing Case misses its deadline, it must automatically be reassigned from the junior analyst's Worklist to the senior compliance manager, without the junior analyst doing anything.' How is this implemented in Pega?

options.text: Configure a Deadline escalation action 'Reassign' that specifies the senior compliance manager as the new assignee — the reassignment fires automatically when the deadline passes
The junior analyst must manually reassign the Case from their Worklist when they see the urgency increase; Pega cannot reassign without user action
Configure a Decision Table that detects the deadline has passed and routes the Case to the manager's Work Queue via a routing rule in the next Step
Set the SLA's 'Auto-close on deadline' flag and configure the manager as the next assignee; the deadline closes the current Assignment and opens a new one for the manager

practiceQuiz.hint: The requirement is 'automatically reassigned' — which SLA feature handles this without user action?
practiceQuiz.rationale: A configured reassignment action changes the recipient when the deadline event is processed. Reassignment need not depend on the junior analyst’s manual action.

optionExplanations.A: A configured reassignment action changes the recipient when the deadline event is processed.
optionExplanations.B: Reassignment need not depend on the junior analyst’s manual action.
optionExplanations.C: A later Step is not the deadline-triggered reassignment described here.
optionExplanations.D: The proposed auto-close flag is not the documented reassignment configuration.

practiceQuiz.scenario: An SA explains the distinction between the SLA goal/deadline and the passed deadline interval. Which statement is correct?

options.text: Goal and deadline occur once; passed deadline can repeat after the deadline within its configured limit
They are identical — the goal, deadline, and passed deadline interval all refer to the same SLA threshold
The passed deadline interval runs before the goal and deadline — it fires first as an early warning, then the goal fires, then the deadline
The goal is set by the SA; the deadline and passed deadline interval are Pega system defaults that cannot be configured

practiceQuiz.hint: Goal/deadline = one-time thresholds; passed deadline interval = repeating post-deadline cycle.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Goal and deadline are one-time milestones; passed deadline can repeat within configured limits. These are different points and intervals, not the same threshold.

optionExplanations.A: Goal and deadline are one-time milestones; passed deadline can repeat within configured limits.
optionExplanations.B: These are different points and intervals, not the same threshold.
optionExplanations.C: Passed deadline starts after the deadline, not before the goal.
optionExplanations.D: The intervals are configurable rather than fixed system deadlines.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Which escalation action in an SLA can close an overdue Case automatically when business rules require it?

options.text: Resolve the Case — an SLA escalation action can resolve (close) the Case automatically when the threshold fires
Authenticate the user — re-authenticating the user is an escalation action that forces them to log in and complete the work
Refresh a Data Page — refreshing the Data Page clears stale data and causes the workflow to close the Case
Localize the content — switching the UI language is an escalation action that signals the Case can be closed

practiceQuiz.hint: Auto-close an overdue Case = Resolve the Case escalation action.
practiceQuiz.rationale: A configured resolution action can resolve overdue work when that matches the business policy. Authentication does not implement the requested Case resolution.

optionExplanations.A: A configured resolution action can resolve overdue work when that matches the business policy.
optionExplanations.B: Authentication does not implement the requested Case resolution.
optionExplanations.C: Refreshing a Data Page does not itself define this resolution action.
optionExplanations.D: Changing language does not determine the Case outcome.

practiceQuiz.scenario: Why should urgency increases be combined with notification or reassignment escalation actions for managing late work?

options.text: Urgency raises the Assignment's worklist priority while the actions ensure the right people know about and can act on the overdue work
Because urgency increases alone delete the Case — combining them with notifications prevents accidental deletion
To avoid configuring the SLA goal — combining urgency with notifications bypasses the need for a goal threshold
Because Pega requires at least one notification per urgency increase — the system rejects SLAs that increase urgency without a paired notification

practiceQuiz.hint: Urgency = higher priority in queue; notifications/reassignment = humans aware and empowered to act.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Urgency controls priority. Notification and reassignment can supplement it when the business policy requires awareness or a different recipient; they do not guarantee a human response.

optionExplanations.A: Urgency affects prioritization; notification or reassignment can additionally draw attention or change ownership.
optionExplanations.B: Raising urgency does not delete the Case.
optionExplanations.C: Combining actions does not remove the configured goal.
optionExplanations.D: There is no requirement here to pair every increment with a notification.

practiceQuiz.scenario: An incomplete Assignment has a one-hour passed deadline interval, at least three events allowed, and a +5 urgency adjustment. Assuming timely event processing and urgency below the cap, what cycles are scheduled over three hours overdue?

options.text: Three passed deadline cycles, at +1, +2 and +3 hours, each with the configured urgency adjustment
The work automatically completes after 1 hour — the interval is a countdown that resolves the Assignment on expiry
The goal is 1 hour — a passed deadline interval of 1 hour is equivalent to setting the SLA goal to 1 hour
The Case is deleted after 1 hour — an elapsed passed deadline interval triggers Case deletion to free up resources

practiceQuiz.hint: Count overdue intervals separately from the deadline event; check the event limit.
practiceQuiz.rationale: With at least three allowed events and an incomplete Assignment, the scheduled cycles are at +1, +2 and +3 hours. The interval does not inherently complete the work; resolution would need an action.

optionExplanations.A: With at least three allowed events and an incomplete Assignment, the scheduled cycles are at +1, +2 and +3 hours.
optionExplanations.B: The interval does not inherently complete the work; resolution would need an action.
optionExplanations.C: The passed deadline interval is measured after the deadline, not from the goal.
optionExplanations.D: A recurring event does not inherently delete the Case.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A BA is configuring an SLA for a high-volume claims process and wants late assignments to keep escalating after the initial deadline passes. How can a passed deadline interval be configured to repeat the escalation?

options.text: A fixed number of times, OR until the user completes the Assignment — each repeat can raise Urgency and send an escalation Action
It always repeats forever and cannot be limited
It fires exactly once, like the goal and deadline
Only until the goal is reached, then it stops

practiceQuiz.hint: Passed deadline interval offers two repeat options: count-based or completion-based.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Repeat policy can limit events or continue while the Assignment remains incomplete. A finite event count can cap repetition; it is not necessarily endless.

optionExplanations.A: Repeat policy can limit events or continue while the Assignment remains incomplete.
optionExplanations.B: A finite event count can cap repetition; it is not necessarily endless.
optionExplanations.C: A repeatable passed deadline schedule differs from the one-time milestones.
optionExplanations.D: The overdue schedule occurs after the deadline, not until the earlier goal.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A junior developer cannot find the passed deadline interval configuration in App Studio while setting up an SLA that must repeat an escalation email after the deadline passes. An SA explains that this setting is only available in one specific studio. In which studio is the passed deadline interval configured, and on which Rule?

options.text: Only in Dev Studio, on the Service-Level Agreement Rule (App Studio's SLA creates that Rule)
Only in App Studio, on the Goal & deadline panel
In Admin Studio's scheduling console
In Prediction Studio

practiceQuiz.hint: App Studio exposes goal/deadline; the passed deadline interval needs the Rule.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The documented procedure opens the SLA Rule in Dev Studio for passed deadline configuration. The App Studio goal/deadline panel links to the Rule rather than exposing this interval there.

optionExplanations.A: The documented procedure opens the SLA Rule in Dev Studio for passed deadline configuration.
optionExplanations.B: The App Studio goal/deadline panel links to the Rule rather than exposing this interval there.
optionExplanations.C: The procedure does not use the runtime scheduling console to author this SLA Rule.
optionExplanations.D: Prediction Studio is not the documented SLA configuration tool.

practiceQuiz.scenario: An Assignment's Urgency is already 100 when its deadline passes, and the SLA is set to notify the manager. What happens?

options.text: Pega ignores the Urgency increment (it is capped at 100) but STILL sends the notification
The notification is suppressed because Urgency cannot increase further
Urgency rises above 100 to force the notification
The Case is auto-resolved because Urgency hit the maximum

practiceQuiz.hint: Max Urgency = 100; what still runs at the cap?
practiceQuiz.rationale: The urgency adjustment is capped, while the configured notification action still runs. The cap does not suppress other configured actions.

optionExplanations.A: The urgency adjustment is capped, while the configured notification action still runs.
optionExplanations.B: The cap does not suppress other configured actions.
optionExplanations.C: Urgency does not exceed 100 to deliver an action.
optionExplanations.D: Reaching maximum urgency is not automatic Case resolution.

practiceQuiz.scenario: An SLA is attached and its deadline event was processed. Inspection shows no passed deadline interval or notification action configured. What must be added for recurring manager notifications after the deadline?

options.text: Configure a passed deadline interval and its notification action on the existing SLA Rule
The SLA rule is not attached to the case type, so deadline tracking never started
Urgency cannot increase beyond the deadline value by design
The Pega scheduler is paused, preventing all time-based rules from executing

practiceQuiz.hint: Use the inspected configuration rather than diagnosing a scheduler fault from a missing email.
practiceQuiz.rationale: A passed deadline schedule and its actions must be configured for this repeated notification. The scenario confirms an attached SLA and processed deadline, so missing attachment is not the stated problem.

optionExplanations.A: A passed deadline schedule and its actions must be configured for this repeated notification.
optionExplanations.B: The scenario confirms an attached SLA and processed deadline, so missing attachment is not the stated problem.
optionExplanations.C: Further increases are possible below 100; the deadline value is not a separate ceiling.
optionExplanations.D: The stated configuration evidence does not establish a paused scheduler.

practiceQuiz.scenario: An incomplete Assignment has a two-hour passed deadline interval with at least three events allowed. Assuming timely processing, how many passed deadline events are scheduled in seven hours overdue?

options.text: 3 times — at hours 2, 4, and 6 past the deadline
4 times — the deadline itself counts as the first firing
1 time — interval fires once and stops until manually reset
0 times — interval rules require operator action to trigger

practiceQuiz.hint: Count +2, +4 and +6 hours; the deadline event is separate.
practiceQuiz.rationale: With at least three events allowed, scheduled overdue intervals occur at +2, +4 and +6 hours. The deadline event is separate and does not count as the first passed deadline interval.

optionExplanations.A: With at least three events allowed, scheduled overdue intervals occur at +2, +4 and +6 hours.
optionExplanations.B: The deadline event is separate and does not count as the first passed deadline interval.
optionExplanations.C: The interval is repeatable, subject to the configured count and completion.
optionExplanations.D: These SLA events do not require a user click to trigger each scheduled cycle.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A Pega developer asks about the passed deadline interval on an SLA rule. Which TWO statements are true about how the passed deadline interval works?

options.text: The passed deadline interval is configured only in Dev Studio on the SLA Rule, not in App Studio
The interval can be set to repeat a fixed number of times or to repeat until the work completes
The passed deadline interval fires before the deadline as an early warning mechanism
Each firing of the passed deadline interval resets the Case Urgency back to zero

practiceQuiz.hint: Recall where passed deadline is configured and what its repeat options are — it fires after the deadline, not before.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The passed deadline configuration is on the SLA Rule in Dev Studio. Events can be limited to a count or continue while the Assignment remains incomplete.

optionExplanations.A: The passed deadline configuration is on the SLA Rule in Dev Studio.
optionExplanations.B: Events can be limited to a count or continue while the Assignment remains incomplete.
optionExplanations.C: Passed deadline occurs after the deadline, not as a pre-deadline warning.
optionExplanations.D: An interval does not inherently reset urgency to zero.

practiceQuiz.scenario: An SA is explaining SLA urgency behavior during escalation to a junior developer. Which TWO statements correctly describe how urgency is managed in Pega SLAs?

options.text: The maximum urgency value in Pega is capped at 100 and cannot be exceeded
Urgency increments can be configured separately for the goal, deadline, and passed deadline intervals
Urgency values above 100 are automatically converted into email notifications
Case Urgency and Assignment Urgency are always identical and cannot differ

practiceQuiz.hint: Remember the hard urgency ceiling and that each SLA milestone can have its own urgency increment.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Urgency is capped at 100, even if configured increments would otherwise exceed it. Milestones can have their own urgency adjustments.

optionExplanations.A: Urgency is capped at 100, even if configured increments would otherwise exceed it.
optionExplanations.B: Milestones can have their own urgency adjustments.
optionExplanations.C: Excess urgency is not automatically converted to email.
optionExplanations.D: Case priority and Assignment priority are distinct and can differ.

practiceQuiz.scenario: An SA needs a manager notification every 24 hours after the deadline while an Assignment remains incomplete. Which TWO SLA elements define this policy?

options.text: Passed deadline interval set to repeat every 24 hours until the work is completed
An escalation action (Send Notification) configured to fire on each passed deadline interval
A Decision Table to evaluate whether the 24-hour threshold has been reached
A Service Package to route the escalation request to the external email system

practiceQuiz.hint: The two things needed are the repeat interval itself and the action to execute each time it fires.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The overdue interval defines the repeated timing and completion policy. The notification action defines what to do on each applicable interval.

optionExplanations.A: The overdue interval defines the repeated timing and completion policy.
optionExplanations.B: The notification action defines what to do on each applicable interval.
optionExplanations.C: A separate Decision table is not required to time this SLA recurrence.
optionExplanations.D: A Service Package is not the SLA configuration element for this notification policy.

quickRecap.value: Time elapsed SINCE the deadline for a still-open Assignment; defines when to take further action.
Repeat within an event limit or while the Assignment is incomplete; configure the action at each applicable interval.
ONLY in Dev Studio, on the SLA Rule (App Studio SLA creates that Rule).
Max Urgency = 100. At 100, further increments are ignored but other escalation Actions still run (e.g., still notifies).
Notify (assignee/manager/participants) · Reassign (user/Work Queue) · Resolve the Case. Defined with the SLA (SA-M15).
Combine Urgency increases with escalation Actions to drive overdue work to completion.
In the linked 24.2 challenge, adding passed deadline configuration moves subsequent goal/deadline editing to the SLA Rule.
